page: Amazon Web Services r5ad.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz, configured with 4 virtual CPUs across 2 physical cores utilizing symmetric multithreading. System memory totals 32.0 GB of DDR4 operating at 3 GHz, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance includes a bundled 150 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume for high-speed scratch space, baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and no GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate modest computational throughput typical of first-generation EPYC architectures. The server posted a Geekbench multi-core score of 1752.0 and a single-core score of 720.0, placing raw compute output in the lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth registered at 27.27 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 13.18 GB/sec for large-block writes. While synthetic instruction tests like PassMark CPU extended instructions scored low, hardware support for AES and SHA extensions allowed encryption workloads to reach mid-tier PassMark results.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r5ad.xlarge trades high per-core execution speeds for substantial memory density and direct-attached NVMe storage. Workloads that rely on fast local cache or scratch disks avoid the external latency and overhead of network-attached block devices. However, applications bound strictly by integer performance or floating-point compute will encounter performance bottlenecks relative to modern compute-focused alternatives.

The r5ad.xlarge is suited for mid-sized in-memory databases, distributed caching layers such as Redis, batch processing, and data staging pipelines requiring high memory-to-core ratios alongside temporary local storage. Compute-heavy workloads, advanced instruction vectorization, and intensive parallel compilation tasks are ill-suited for this profile.
description: Amazon Web Services r5ad.xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro-based virtual server powered by a 2.2 GHz AMD EPYC 7571 processor with 4 vCPUs and 2 physical cores. It provides 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory, delivering an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio tailored for memory-bound applications. Local storage is provided via a bundled 150 GB NVMe SSD instance volume, alongside a 1 Gbps baseline network interface and zero GPUs. Benchmark scores reflect lower-tier compute and memory bandwidth throughput typical of earlier EPYC architectures, though hardware-assisted cryptography scores in the median range. The instance offers resource density for workloads needing dedicated RAM and high-speed temporary disk space rather than raw processing speed. Workload fit includes in-memory key-value stores, distributed caches, batch processing jobs, and intermediate data staging.
